body: Calling read_csv on an empty file raises an unexpected IndexError instead of returning a clear EmptyDataError. This worked in the previous release.
rationale: Reports broken existing behavior and an unexpected exception.
title: BUG: crash when opening an empty CSV file

body: tz_convert shifts timestamps by one hour around the daylight saving boundary. The output is inconsistent with dateutil for the same timezone.
rationale: Incorrect result for existing timezone behavior.
title: BUG: timezone conversion returns the wrong hour after DST

body: A DataFrame with Int64 columns returns zeros after groupby().sum() when some rows contain NA. Expected the non-null values to be summed.
title: BUG: groupby sum ignores nullable integer column

body: Serializing a DataFrame with a timezone-aware DatetimeIndex fails with TypeError. The same frame serializes correctly after resetting the index.
rationale: Valid existing API path raises an error.
title: BUG: DataFrame.to_json raises TypeError for valid datetime index

body: rolling(3).mean() returns NaN for a window with three numeric values when the Series uses Float64 dtype. Expected a numeric mean.
rationale: Incorrect numerical output for existing rolling operation.
title: BUG: rolling mean produces NaN for complete window

body: Merging two frames on an ordered categorical column produces duplicate rows that are not present when the key is converted to object dtype.
rationale: Existing merge behavior appears wrong for a supported dtype.
title: BUG: merge duplicates rows with categorical key

body: A parquet file written by the library cannot be read back if one column contains a slash in the name. Round-tripping should preserve valid column names.
rationale: Round-trip failure in existing IO behavior.
title: BUG: read_parquet fails on column name containing slash

body: It would be useful to call df.to_schema_json() and get column names, dtypes, nullability, and index metadata for downstream validation tools.
title: ENH: add option to export DataFrame schema as JSON

body: Users currently need to pass regex flags for case-insensitive matching. A boolean ignore_case parameter would make this common operation easier.
rationale: Asks for API improvement rather than reporting broken behavior.
title: ENH: support ignore_case parameter in Series.str.contains

body: For low-memory services it would help if read_csv could yield each chunk as a list of dictionaries without constructing an intermediate DataFrame.
title: ENH: allow read_csv to stream chunks as dictionaries

body: Several libraries call private dtype inference helpers. Could pandas expose a supported infer_dtype_schema function for extension authors?
title: ENH: expose stable public API for dtype inference

body: Concatenating thousands of tiny DataFrames is a bottleneck in ETL jobs. A faster path for homogeneous columns would be valuable.
rationale: Requests performance enhancement, not a correctness bug.
title: ENH: improve performance of concat for many small frames

body: Many finance workflows use fiscal quarters that start in February or April. A dedicated offset type would simplify current custom workarounds.
title: ENH: add native support for fiscal quarter offsets

body: The merge documentation says 'rigth_index' in one example. It should be 'right_index'.
title: DOC: fix typo in DataFrame.merge examples

body: The read_csv page mentions dtype briefly, but the examples do not show passing a mapping from column name to dtype. Adding one would help new users.
title: DOC: clarify that read_csv dtype can accept a dict

body: The contributing guide links to an old Python installation page that now redirects. Please update it to the current Python downloads URL.
title: DOC: outdated link in contributing guide

body: The resample documentation covers calendar days but not business-day frequency. An example with B frequency would make the behavior easier to understand.
title: DOC: add example for resampling with business days

body: Several users are confused that loc includes both slice endpoints while iloc follows Python slicing. The indexing guide should call this out more visibly.
title: DOC: explain difference between loc and iloc for slices

body: The beginner tutorial still shows display.max_colwidth = -1, but that value is deprecated. The example should use None instead.
title: DOC: remove deprecated option from tutorial

body: I have account IDs like 00123 in a CSV. read_csv turns them into integers. What argument should I use to keep them as strings?
title: QST: how do I keep leading zeros when reading CSV?

body: After groupby I get a MultiIndex. Is there a recommended way to turn those index levels back into normal DataFrame columns?
rationale: How-to question about using existing API.
title: QST: can I convert a MultiIndex back into columns?

body: I called df.fillna(0) but the original DataFrame still has missing values. Do I need to assign the result or use another option?
title: QST: why does fillna not modify my DataFrame?

body: For tests I need to compare two DataFrames where floating point values can differ slightly. Is there a built-in helper for this?
title: QST: best way to compare two DataFrames with tolerance

body: My CSV has dates like 2024-01-02 and 01/03/2024 in the same column. Can to_datetime handle this, or should I preprocess first?
title: QST: how to parse mixed date formats in one column?

body: A column has millions of rows but only a few hundred distinct string values. Would category reduce memory, and are there tradeoffs?
rationale: Asks for guidance on using an existing dtype.
title: QST: should I use category dtype for repeated strings?
